title: Bengal Tenancy Act
subtitle: Colonial Bengal's major landlord-tenant law reworked agrarian rights and rent disputes.
summary: The Bengal Tenancy Act of 1885 codified important parts of landlord-tenant relations in Bengal after decades of agrarian conflict and legal uncertainty under the Permanent Settlement framework.
heroTagline: A land law reshaped the terms of peasant, landlord, and colonial authority.
whyItMatters: The act mattered because agrarian rights, occupancy claims, rent enhancement, and litigation shaped rural politics in Bengal well into the twentieth century.
longTermLegacy: The act became a key reference point for later debates over tenancy, peasant protection, and the limits of zamindari authority.
identityMemoryNotes: It belongs to the longer memory of agrarian inequality and legal reform between the Permanent Settlement and later land-reform politics.

claimCitations.claim: The Bengal Tenancy Act of 1885 codified important parts of landlord-tenant relations in Bengal after decades of agrarian conflict and legal uncertainty under the Permanent Settlement framework.
The act mattered because agrarian rights, occupancy claims, rent enhancement, and litigation shaped rural politics in Bengal well into the twentieth century.
The act became a key reference point for later debates over tenancy, peasant protection, and the limits of zamindari authority.
It belongs to the longer memory of agrarian inequality and legal reform between the Permanent Settlement and later land-reform politics.
